description.purpose: The first hive with a domain of its own: the curated record of the people and agents a colony knows. Five cells, no model. `store` holds whole AIeOS 1.1.0 documents in an `aieos` column, everything meclaw adds beside them under `mx`, and the four things AIeOS has no vocabulary for as tables -- relations (cut exactly on the traverse signature), trust, disclosure and an append-only audit. `gate` is the only writer and the only place AIeOS conformance is decided. `brief` is the only reader and the only place the audience filter exists. `push` compares hashes and decides WHETHER a subscriber hears anything; `clock` ticks it. Memory produces, affinity decides -- and only affinity is quoted when the answer is `who is X to me`.
description.use_when: Once per family or org tree, as a sibling of the agents rather than inside one, because an agent's persona and a person's record are the same document in this hive and both are read by several agents. Wire the two ports in the same mutation as the add_nodes. The brief ingress MUST deliver the asker AND the round (`hop.audience` + `hop.audience_set`, which the door edge promotes to `context.asker` / `context.audience_set` -- or the same two keys promoted on the caller's own edge) and the propose ingress MUST promote the writer to `context.actor` and, for `subscribe`, the subscribing cell's address to `context.subscriber`: these cells take identity from the edge and never from body text, because a body is model-writable and an edge is not. Precedence at the door is edge-pinned first (`context.asker` -> `hop.audience` -> '' for the asker, `context.audience_set` -> `hop.audience_set` -> '' for the round), so a cell downstream of the pinning edge cannot shrink its own room by stamping a hop key. `context.participants` was this hive's internal name for the round until GH #330; it is retired, not aliased -- a request that declares its round only under the old name is refused `no_round`, and no template may ever introduce a second name for it. A request that declares no round at all is refused the same way (GH #306) -- reading it as the asker alone is the WIDEST reading a subset test can be given, not the narrowest. Identity references inside the round are affinity's alone to mint and map (UUID-backed here, byte-identical on the wire); receptionist, memory and talky only transport them and never resolve them.
description.not_in_scope: No LLM, and no human either: nothing in this hive reads a proposal in order to judge it. A memory-born proposal lands in `proposals` with status `accepted` and the actor the edge named as `decided_by` -- R-AF-1, because the safety net is the substrate rather than a queue somebody has to work through: no branch of `gate` ever emits `delete`, and a verdict appends instead of overwriting the row it judged. `auto_accept: false` is the exception a caller asks for deliberately; that row lands `open` and waits for a later `decide_proposal`. No name resolution (a subject is an entity_id), no per-turn recall (that stays the direct collector-to-memory wire) and no encryption at rest. And sovereignty is enforced only in half: the substrate refuses a write from outside the hive (`write_denied`, from the store's `write_surface: "internal"`) and refuses a mutation that names a path inside it (`hive_port_boundary`), but a parent's BOOT graph may wire straight into `./store` and a read from anywhere is free -- the audience filter lives in `./brief`, after the read. The audit table makes a bypass visible afterwards; nothing prevents it.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty; an edge naming ./brief, ./gate or ./push is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route. in_brief: an edge into the HIVE carrying the request as a tool_call turn ({subject, channel, slots}) plus the asker and the round on the hop (hop.audience, hop.audience_set), which the door edge promotes to context.asker and context.audience_set -- `participants` is retired, not aliased (GH #330), so a request that spells the round that way declared no round at all; a missing or unknown asker (no_audience) and an undeclared round (no_round) both get an answer with NO system slot at all; the door also resets aff_phase/aff_carry/aff_subscriber so a fresh request cannot inherit a lane. out_brief: the hive path on hop.route=='answer' && hop.subscriber=='' into the asking llm cell -- system.identity|peer|relationship|channel, each a renderable leaf, plus a tool_result carrying the receipt line, that same pack as JSON (a sealed agent hive drops the system slot on its tool lane) and the id of the call being answered. in_propose: an edge into the HIVE on the write side, promoting the writer to context.actor and, for subscribe, the subscribing cell's address to context.subscriber -- the subscription row is an ADDRESS the hive's push lane reads every tick, so a body that names cell_path or audience is refused with identity_from_body (GH #288). out_ack: the hive path on hop.route=='ack' back to the proposer (accepted|rejected plus a reason_code). out_push: the hive path on hop.route=='answer' && hop.subscriber=='<cell path>' into each subscribed llm cell -- system.* and no turn beside it, so the slot update costs the subscriber a write and not an inference (GH #263). The parent draws ONE such edge per subscribing cell at instantiation and conditions it on that cell's own path: a subscribe writes a row, never an edge (mutation authority is the colony's), so a subscription with no edge behind it is accepted and undeliverable. The out_brief edge in the same graph MUST carry hop.subscriber=='' or it collects every push as well -- brief stamps subscriber on EVERY answer emission, the tool lane as the empty string, so the emptiness is a value and not an absence (GH #289). out_error: the hive path on hop.route=='error' into a drain the parent MUST wire.

attune once per agent birth: affinity_brief{subject:'entity:aiden'} over the boot lane -> system.identity from the AGENT's own AIeOS document, accumulated in the llm cell's cell.db per slot path; every slot carries a `text` rendering beside its structure, because an llm cell concatenates `text` leaves into the prompt and renders nothing else (GH #258)

a person the audience has three disclosure rows for -> exactly those three fields; the same person for an audience with no row -> the document is never even read, one audit row says denied, and the answer carries nothing
who is Sam to Alex: ONE traverse op over `relations`, two hops, answered by the store instead of by a graph walk in a script
a curated correction: gate marks the active row superseded and inserts the new one -- no delete is ever emitted, so the previous record stays readable

push-on-change: every tick hashes what each subscriber WOULD get; unchanged means zero messages, changed means exactly one re-brief through ./brief, so the audience filter can only be wrong in one place
